clue.text: Bombers, say, display cunning

parts.note: to air something is to show or display it publicly
craft is cunning or guile

explanation.surface: Warplanes show off their guile.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombers are one example of flying machines, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Kidnap seaman on canal

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a duct is a tube or canal in the body

explanation.surface: A sailor is snatched on a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force.

clue.text: Send back into custody chap in debt?

indicators.note: in places the chap piece inside the debt piece

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Should a man in debt be returned to jail?
explanation.definitionFit: To remand a prisoner is to return them to custody pending trial.

clue.text: Figure caught in shipwreck once

indicators.note: caught in means the letters are found within these words

explanation.surface: Someone estimates what was trapped in an old wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to calculate or estimate.

clue.text: Order written out (without reference to leader) in battle

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the battle word

parts.note: a fray is a fight or battle

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
the leader is the first letter, which is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: A command is written up, leaving out the general, during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without reference to leader' drops the first letter of 'written', and 'out' rearranges what is left into TERNIT; 'in' then sets that inside the battle word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood or religious order is a fraternity.

clue.text: One may bring good fortune in maiden on racecourse

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: A lucky charm brought along by a young woman at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring luck.

clue.text: Rotter with loose mice H N R L R chasing a scholar

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the rest comes after the single letter
with joins the rotter piece to the following letters

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man

indicators.note: loose means let free, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scoundrel with escaped mice chases a learned person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges MICE as EMIC. The letters H N R L R are stray printing marks, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a university scholar or teacher.

clue.text: Semi Tripe, cold piece friend brought over brought over

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a piece
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Rubbish: a cold slice of tripe served to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns PARTPAL into LAPTRAP. The stray 'Semi' and repeated 'brought over' are printing faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is nonsense, the same as calling it tripe.

clue.text: Hypotheses produced by rightwinger entertaining ambassador

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Tories are right-wing British Conservatives
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: Theories put forward by a Conservative hosting a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambassadors are addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE; 'entertaining' sets that inside the right-wingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are hypotheses, ideas put forward to explain facts.

clue.text: Blackleg on march ahead of Conservative party member

indicators.note: on, in a down-the-line reading, places the strike-breaker after the rest
ahead of puts the march piece before the Conservative piece

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
a rat is a strike-breaker, also called a blackleg

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker on a protest march leads a Tory party member.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is British slang for a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Democratic Party is so named.

clue.text: Handle husband with maturity

parts.note: a woman's man is her husband
age means maturity, years of experience

explanation.surface: Coping with a husband as he grows older.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage something is to handle or cope with it.

clue.text: Overlooked swindle perpetrated by daughter

parts.note: a con is a swindle
done means carried out, perpetrated

explanation.surface: A fraud carried out by a daughter was ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone a wrong is to overlook or excuse it.

clue.text: Priam's son, a blustering bully

definitions.meaning: the Trojan prince killed by Achilles, eldest son of King Priam in the Iliad
a noun for a swaggering person who intimidates others

explanation.surface: A Trojan prince is described as an overbearing bully.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan hero of Homer's Iliad lent his name to a swaggering bully, from his portrayal in later drama.

clue.text: Edberg's first tennis stroke, after bit of bother earlier calico un

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its opening letter
first picks out the opening letter of the tennis player's name

parts.note: a forehand is a tennis stroke

explanation.surface: Stefan Edberg's opening forehand came after some trouble earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the B of bother first. Edberg was a Swedish tennis champion. The trailing 'calico un' is a printing fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Beforehand means in advance, earlier.

clue.text: Embarrassing point about the Spanish

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to indicate is to point out
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Pointing at the Spanish is an awkward thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the pointing word go around the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indelicate is tactless or improper, causing embarrassment.

clue.text: Mounted, jumps with the nouveaux riches

parts.note: up means mounted, on horseback
starts are sudden jumps

explanation.surface: Riders who leap about among the newly wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstarts are people newly risen in wealth or status who behave arrogantly.

clue.text: Equestrian — husky fellow, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken and the sound gives the entry

parts.note: a man with a husky voice is a hoarse man

explanation.surface: A rider described as a gruff-voiced chap, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian is a rider on horseback.

clue.text: Meteors crashed enveloping southern county

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping around one piece
crashed means smashed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shooting stars crashed down around a county in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges METEORS; 'enveloping' puts S inside. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county in the West Country.

clue.text: Relationship with president prior to moving on?

indicators.note: moving means these letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking about a link with the president before he moves on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'moving on' is a politician leaving office; 'moving' instead shuffles 'prior to' to ROPORTI. P for president is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportion is the ratio or relation of one part to another.

clue.text: Run into son on three-wheeler

parts.note: a trike is a tricycle, a three-wheeler

explanation.surface: Colliding with a boy on a tricycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike something is to hit or run into it.

clue.text: Youth (particularly handsome) a lecturer is after

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man is the target of a lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was a beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite; the name now means any handsome young man.

clue.text: International edition is critically examined

parts.note: a Test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: An edition of an international match is scrutinised.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Tested means tried out or put through careful scrutiny.

clue.text: Performance during act is subdued

indicators.note: during means the first piece sits within the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
a feat is a notable performance or achievement

explanation.surface: A show performed in the middle of an act is muted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' sets the performance inside the act; 'is' merely links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be defeated is to be beaten or overcome.

clue.text: Thoughtless concerning young lady

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Careless remarks about a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless in one's duty.

clue.text: Holiday with Virginia and Prudence, not suitable for the children?

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out of the word

parts.note: caution means prudence
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, fit for children

explanation.surface: A break with two women named Virginia and Prudence that is unfit for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes U, the British film rating for films anyone may see, from CAUTION to leave CATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacation is a holiday, a break from work or study.

clue.text: Ancient Roman assembly depicted in a tense novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Roman council portrayed in a tense work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman council of elders governed the Republic.

clue.text: Newspaper boss, English, wearing appalling strides article

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the trousers piece is around the English letter
appalling means dreadful, so these letters are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A female editor, English, dons dreadful trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Strides is British slang for trousers; 'appalling' rearranges STRIDES and 'wearing' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a female editor, the head of a newspaper.
